tooltip.title: Central Question
tooltip.markdown: The core goal is to investigate a chronic, recalcitrant skin rash that could be Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma (CTCL). The workup follows a logical path from suspicion to diagnosis, staging, and establishing prognosis.

tooltip.title: Question 1: What is it?
tooltip.markdown: The first step is to confirm the diagnosis of CTCL and determine its specific subtype through a careful integration of clinical, pathologic, and molecular findings.

tooltip.title: Skin Biopsy (Histopathology)
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** The cornerstone of diagnosis. Multiple biopsies from different areas may be needed.
-   **Key MF/SS Features:** A superficial infiltrate of **atypical lymphocytes** with cerebriform nuclei.
-   **Epidermotropism:** Atypical lymphocytes infiltrating the epidermis without significant spongiosis (inflammation).
-   **Pautrier Microabscesses:** Intraepidermal clusters of atypical lymphocytes; pathognomonic but not always present.
-   **Other signs:** Linear alignment of lymphocytes at the dermal-epidermal junction ("tagging"), haloed lymphocytes, lymphoid atypia.

tooltip.title: TCR Gene Rearrangement (Skin)
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** Detects a dominant T-cell population (a clone), which supports a diagnosis of lymphoma.
-   **Method:** PCR or High-Throughput Sequencing (HTS) of the T-cell receptor (TCR) gamma chain gene.
-   **Interpretation:** A positive result (monoclonality) supports CTCL, but is **not diagnostic alone**, as reactive conditions and elderly individuals can sometimes have benign clones. An identical clone in two distinct skin sites is more specific for CTCL.

tooltip.title: Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** Stains for specific cell surface markers to determine the lineage and characteristics of the infiltrate.
-   **Key Markers in MF/SS:** Typically CD3+, CD4+, CD8-, CD5+, with loss of CD7.
-   **CD30:** Important for identifying CD30+ LPDs and large-cell transformation in MF. Large-cell transformation is a morphologic diagnosis (large cells ≥25% of the infiltrate or forming nodules) and can be CD30-positive or CD30-negative; CD30 alone neither establishes nor excludes it.

tooltip.title: Question 2: How bad is it?
tooltip.markdown: Once diagnosed, staging determines the extent of disease, which is the most important prognostic factor. This involves assessing skin, blood, lymph node, and visceral involvement.

tooltip.title: Complete Skin Exam
tooltip.markdown: Assess the type of lesions (patch, plaque, tumor) and calculate the Body Surface Area (BSA) involved to determine the T-stage.

tooltip.title: Staging Blood Work
tooltip.markdown: To assess for systemic involvement (B-stage). Includes CBC with differential, comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP), and LDH.

tooltip.title: Peripheral Blood Flow Cytometry
tooltip.markdown: The key test to quantify blood involvement. It identifies and counts the number of malignant Sézary cells to determine the B-stage.

tooltip.title: Staging Imaging
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Purpose:** To evaluate for lymph node and visceral involvement (N and M stages).
-   **Method:** Typically a contrast-enhanced CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis. PET/CT may be used for aggressive disease or suspected transformation.

tooltip.title: Lymph Node Biopsy
tooltip.markdown: If clinically enlarged lymph nodes are present, an excisional biopsy is performed to pathologically stage the nodes (N-stage).
